newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Major calls for "credible" IRA truce.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Major calls for "credible" IRA truce.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Tuesday called on the IRA to declare "a credible ceasefire" in its battle to drive Britain from Northern Ireland.
"Call a ceasefire and make it a credible ceasefire," Major, speaking in parliament, urged the IRA. "IRA terrorism is utterly unacceptable for any purpose, at any time, in any place."

A response is awaited from Major to proposals put forward last week by Northern Ireland Catholic politician John Hume and the Irish Republican Army's political wing, Sinn Fein, as preconditions for resuming a ceasefire abandoned in February.
Under the proposals, Sinn Fein would be allowed into talks on the future of Northern Ireland once the truce was called.
Hume, as leader of the moderately Irish nationalist Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP), has been heavily involved in efforts to get Sinn Fein included in the multi-party talks.
Hume and Sinn Fein want a rigid timetable for the talks, chaired by former U.S. senator George Mitchell. They say British demands that the guerrillas disarm first should be dropped.
They also want confidence-building measures, such as the release of IRA prisoners.
Sinn Fein has been barred from joining the talks because of the IRA's refusal to renew its 17-month ceasefire.
Their pro-British "Loyalist" rivals have been allowed to join the talks, sponsored by London and Dublin, because their guerrillas have stuck to a two-year-old truce.
